head: Firefox 160 update: Mini Window, video speed in picture-in-picture
dek: Firefox 160 lets you pop a tab, or part of a page, into a small window that stays on top while you work in other windows. The picture-in-picture player also gets a playback speed setting from 0.25x to 2x.
details: Mozilla calls Mini Window an early version and asks for feedback. A new Never allow button stops sites that keep asking to open email (mailto) and other links in outside apps; you can manage blocked sites in Settings. Picture-in-picture shows the speed setting only when its window is medium-sized or larger. You can also drag history from the sidebar onto the tab strip, and Firefox now plays MKV files with FLAC, MP3 or PCM audio.
where: Out since 10 November for Firefox on Windows, Mac and Linux
means: If you watch tutorials or lectures in Firefox, you can speed them up or slow them down in the floating player, and keep a page in view while you work elsewhere.
todo: Update Firefox to version 160. Next time a site keeps asking to open your mail app, pick Never allow.
